label: Tuition fee (non-EU/EEA, English-taught degrees)
notes: Non-EU/EEA students in English-taught bachelor's and master's programmes pay tuition, typically EUR 9,000-20,000 per year depending on the university and programme. EU/EEA students and doctoral programmes are tuition-free. Individual programme fees on our catalogue come from each implementation's own record.

provenance.source: Study in Finland - Fees and Cost of Living

label: Living costs
notes: The Finnish Immigration Service (Migri) minimum is EUR 800 per month (EUR 9,600 per year); the official portal recommends budgeting roughly EUR 900-1,200 per month depending on location, with Helsinki and southern cities pricier. This is money you live on, not a fee you pay to anyone.

provenance.source: Study in Finland - Fees and Cost of Living (incl. Migri minimum)

label: Student healthcare fee and student union fee
notes: University students pay the FSHS healthcare fee of about EUR 35 per term (about EUR 70 per year) plus a student union fee of about EUR 50-70 per academic year. Students at universities of applied sciences arrange private insurance instead, which varies in price.

provenance.source: Study in Finland - Fees and Cost of Living
